recipes.name: Deluxe Ham Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of celery soup

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook macaroni in boiling water uncovered, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes; drain.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir ham and onion in hot butter until onion is tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook for about 2 minutes more; remove the skillet from heat.
Add macaroni, Cheddar cheese, condensed soup, peas, milk, sour cream, onion powder, and garlic powder to ham mixture in the skillet; mix until well combined.
Transfer mixture to the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is melted, about 25 minutes.
Sprinkle French-fried onions over casserole and continue baking until golden, about 5 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Deluxe Ham Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This ham casserole features elbow macaroni baked in a comforting creamy sauce with ham, peas, and Cheddar cheese, topped with crispy onions.

review.reviewBody: I use frozen broccoli in place of the peas and cream of chicken in place of the cream of celery. The leftovers from this casserole rewarm well, if there's any leftover. NOTE: If you don't have ham, this is also good with tuna fish or leftover rotisserie chicken.

Great use for leftover ham. I doubled the amount of ham called for in the recipe and next time would double the peas as well. Used cream of mushroom soup instead of celery because that was what I had on hand. I covered it with foil while baking to avoid the crunchy noodle problem, kept foil off after added onion ring topping to brown. Easy and a hit with the family!

I was in a hurry, so I didn't sautee' onions and garlic. I just used the spices. Used skim milk and fat free sour cream and instead of Cheddar, used Colby Jack. This was delicious and I will definitely make again, but next time I will follow the directions and it should be even better! Hope you try this one and enjoy it as much as I did. I didn't use the french-fried onions, either,but will the next time :-)

Delicious! Important tips: 1) don't forget to salt the pasta water, 2) don't overcook the pasta since it will cook some more in the oven and 3) add about 1 tsp of salt to creamy mixture. I put in frozen broccoli florets and added crumbled bacon/ cracker topping on top. It was ah-mazing. My husband, who doesn't like casserole type dishes, went back for seconds. :)

I've been making this recipe for over 60 years. It was one the first one's I learned. I've changed out the soups (mushroom, celery, chicken etc ) at different times a long with the vegetables (corn, mixed veggies, carrots etc). I have also tried different meats (turkey, tuna, browned beef). Try using bread crumbs on top, rather than onions. This recipe is so easy, versatile and inexpensive to make. I highly recommend any girl (or boy) learning to cook, add it to their recipe box. Excellent for Church Pot Lucks too.

Followed the recipe, the only thing changed was I used rotini instead of macaroni. Also only put 1/2 tablespoon of garlic as we don't like strong garlic favors. I love peas, and I love ham, and I love combining the two. I didn't want it to dry out in the oven as some other reviewers mentioned this happening, so I covered it with foil taking it off when I put on the French fried onions. It came out of the oven with just the right consistency. So I'm wondering if the reviewers that had issues with it being to dry maybe substituted the frozen peas with a non-frozen veggie. I'm thinking that the frozen peas let off moisture as they thaw and bake. Maybe, maybe not? It is a tad on the salty side, but not so much that it is unpalatable. My hubby who tends to more frequently voice his opinion if he doesn't like something, said "it was good" and he "liked it" and that is about as enthusiastic as it gets from him. So I think this recipe was tasty and will probably be made again.

I would recommend 1 1/2 cups ham and 1 3/4 cup peas. Substituted the cheddar for swiss. Definitely a new staple. Kids love it. They said dinner smelt good as soon as they walked in the door. After the official taste test two thumbs up.

Okay, my family loved this casserole. I picked this recipe cause I needed to clear a few items out of the freezer. So obviously my review is based on my needed changes! Leftover ham,
broccoli (instead of peas) and leftover veggie dip(instead of sour cream) 
TIP: Since I hate to waste food I always freeze any leftover sour cream based dips to use in recipes later.
Very tasty and great for leftover ham! I halved the recipe, except for added a full can of soup and a full cup of peas. I also used fusilli noodles. My family liked it a lot!

One of the tastiest casseroles I have ever eaten. Followed the recipe except had no celery soup and used mushroom soup instead, but it was wonderful......my husband is so happy that there is asome left over and he can eat it again tomorrow when I am at a meeting......lucky guy.
I did not have cream of celery soup on hand so I used creamed corn the taste is yummy before I even cooked it.
Made this recipe today. Did not change anything. My husband and I really enjoyed it. Will be making this again.

Made this casserole as directed. It is a keeper for us. Very easy to make and it is delicious! I used Rotini pasta instead of elbows. It's just me and hubby so I used two smaller casserole dishes and froze one for later. This does freeze well, as long as you do not bake it before you freeze it. We had the first one last week and the frozen one tonight. I just defrosted it before heating up. I love salt, but did not think this was too salty. You can always use unsalted butter and maybe a lower sodium ham if you want to cut back on the salt. Thanks for the recipe!

It tasted fine, but is a little boring. May try using sharper cheese or adding some Dijon next time. Glad I added extra ham and peas as recommended or it would have just been basically a creamy macaroni.

This recipe was a home run. I was going to host two families and was looking for a winner casserole recipe and this one was a life saver. The rich, creamy texture and the layered, delicious flavors were enjoyed bu everyone; so much so that they all came back for seconds.
Our family loved this as is. My husband put some queso sauce on the leftovers and said it was amazing. So he told me to have it on hand for next time.

I diced up the ham and onion and sauteed put in greenbean casserole and cream of chicken soup added garlic,dry musturd pepper milk and sharp cheese. topping I used some smashed fritos and bread crumbs and topped with cheddar
Great Flavor! Perfect use of leftover ham.
Used 2 cups leftover spiral ham. This was a creamy delicious Mac and Cheese.

This was tasty, but lacking. The noodles were actually kind of crunchy when coming out of the oven, which neither my husband or I really cared for. (Note: I used condensed cheddar cheese soup instead of cream of celery; that might have affected the creaminess of the dish, but I really don't think so). If I make again, I will increase the amount of ham, soup and chopped onion. I think I will add some dry mustard to the recipe also. The French fried onions were a nice touch. With the changes, this might go to a 4 or 5 star rating. FYI: this reheats very nicely in the microwave, and with some EverythingBagel seasoning added, the flavor improves a lot.
